\( i_{\mathrm{rms}} = 5 \) A, so the peak current is \( i_0 = \sqrt{2}\, i_{\mathrm{rms}} = 5\sqrt{2} \) A. Measuring time from the instant the current is zero and rising, \( i = i_0 \sin \omega t \) with \( \omega = 2\pi f = 100\pi \) rad/s.
At \( t = \frac{1}{300} \) s, \( \omega t = \frac{100\pi}{300} = \frac{\pi}{3} \), so \( \sin \omega t = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \).
\( i = 5\sqrt{2} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 5\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} = 6.124 \) A.
Discrimination — each of the other three values fails a test of its own. The value \( 5\sqrt{2} = 7.071 \) A is the PEAK current, which is reached only at \( \omega t = \pi/2 \), i.e. at \( t = 1/200 \) s, not at \( t = 1/300 \) s. The value \( 5/\sqrt{2} = 3.536 \) A divides the rms current by \( \sqrt{2} \) instead of multiplying by it. The value \( 5/6 = 0.833 \) A corresponds to nothing derivable from the given data. Only \( 5\sqrt{3/2} = 6.124 \) A matches the computed instantaneous current, so the correct option is B.

Comparing \( V = 100\sqrt{2} \sin (1000\, t) \) with \( V = V_0 \sin \omega t \) gives \( \omega = 1000 \) rad/s.
\( X_L = \omega L = 1000 \times 0.5 = 500\ \Omega \), which equals \( R = 500\ \Omega \).
\( Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2} = \sqrt{500^2 + 500^2} = 500\sqrt{2}\ \Omega \).
Power factor \( \cos\phi = \frac{R}{Z} = \frac{500}{500\sqrt{2}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 0.707 \).
Discrimination — because \( X_L = R \) exactly, \( \phi = 45^\circ \) and the power factor can only be \( 1/\sqrt{2} \). The value \( 1/\sqrt{3} = 0.577 \) would require \( X_L = \sqrt{2}\,R \), the value \( 0.5 \) would require \( X_L = \sqrt{3}\,R \), and the value \( 0.6 \) would require \( X_L = \frac{4}{3}R \); the given \( \omega L \) produces none of these. Hence the power factor is \( 1/\sqrt{2} \) and the correct option is A.

The current LEADS the voltage, so the circuit is capacitance dominated and \( X_C > X_L \).
\( \tan 45^\circ = \frac{X_C - X_L}{R} = 1 \), so \( X_C = X_L + R = 2\pi f L + R \).
Since \( X_C = \frac{1}{2\pi f C} \),
\( C = \frac{1}{2\pi f X_C} = \frac{1}{2\pi f \left( 2\pi f L + R \right)} \).
Discrimination, in two independent steps. (1) The SIGN: the two expressions carrying \( \left( 2\pi f L - R \right) \) are what you obtain when the current LAGS, so they answer the opposite question and are excluded by the word "leads" in the stem. (2) The COEFFICIENT: the two expressions carrying \( \pi f \) rather than \( 2\pi f \) drop the factor 2 in \( X_C = 1/(2\pi f C) \) and are out by exactly a factor of 2. Only \( \frac{1}{2\pi f \left( 2\pi f L + R \right)} \) survives both tests.
Checked numerically with \( f = 60 \) Hz, \( L = 0.30 \) H, \( R = 40\ \Omega \): this expression gives \( C = 1.7326 \times 10^{-5} \) F, and feeding that back gives \( X_C - X_L = 40.00\ \Omega = R \), i.e. a phase angle of exactly \( 45^\circ \) with the current leading. The other three expressions give \( 7.258 \times 10^{-5} \), \( 3.629 \times 10^{-5} \) and \( 3.465 \times 10^{-5} \) F, for which \( X_C - X_L \) comes out as \( -76.55 \), \( -40.00 \) and \( -36.55\ \Omega \) — every one of them a LAGGING current, so none reproduces the stated \( 45^\circ \) lead. The correct option is D.

\( e_0 = 150 \) V and \( i_0 = 150 \) A, and the phase difference between them is \( \phi = \frac{\pi}{3} \), so \( \cos\phi = 0.5 \).
\( P_{\mathrm{av}} = e_{\mathrm{rms}}\, i_{\mathrm{rms}} \cos\phi = \frac{e_0}{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \frac{i_0}{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \cos\phi = \frac{e_0 i_0}{2} \cos\phi \)
\( = \frac{150 \times 150}{2} \times 0.5 = 11250 \times 0.5 = 5625 \) W.
Discrimination — a value of zero would require \( \phi = 90^\circ \), i.e. a purely reactive circuit, whereas here \( \phi = 60^\circ \). The value 150 W is simply the amplitude carried over with no computation. The value 106 W is \( 150/\sqrt{2} = 106.07 \), the rms of 150, which is a current or a voltage and not a power at all. Note that \( e_0 i_0 = 22500 \) W is the peak instantaneous product and \( e_0 i_0 / 2 = 11250 \) W would be the answer if the two were in phase; the factor \( \cos 60^\circ = 0.5 \) halves it again to 5625 W. Only 5625 W is consistent, so the correct option is C.

Power factor is by definition \( \cos\phi \), where \( \phi \) is the phase difference between the applied voltage and the current.
\( \cos 45^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 0.7071 \).
Discrimination — a power factor of 1 belongs to resonance, where \( \phi = 0 \), not \( 45^\circ \). The values 0.607 and 0.808 correspond to \( \phi = 52.6^\circ \) and \( \phi = 36.1^\circ \) respectively, neither of which is the stated angle. Only 0.707 equals \( \cos 45^\circ \), so the correct option is B.
